title: Protocol for Biochemical Analysis and Structure Determination of the ZZ Domain of the E3 Ubiquitin Ligase HERC2
protocol: Transform the expression plasmids that encode HERC2ZZ, H31–6-HERC2ZZ, SUMO11–6-HERC2ZZ and full-length SUMO into BL21 (DE3) RIL chemically competent cells following the protocol described above.
Plate transformed cells onto LB agar plates supplemented with 34 μg/mL chloramphenicol and 100 μg/mL kanamycin for HERC2ZZ or ampicillin for pDEST-15 SUMO1.
Inoculate a single colony into 200 mL LB media supplemented with corresponding antibiotics.
Culture cells in an orbital incubator shaker at 37°C and 200 rpm, for 14–18 hours.
Dilute the overnight culture 1:100 in 2L LB media supplemented with chloramphenicol, kanamycin, and ZnCl2.
Culture the cells at 37°C with agitation speed of 200 rpm until optical density reaches 0.6–0.8 at an absorbance of 600.
Reduce shaker temperature to 16°C and speed to 180 rpm while cooling down the cell culture for 30 min to 23°C-25°C.
Induce protein expression by adding IPTG, along with agitation and incubation at 16°C for 20 h.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 5,000 rpm (4,424 × g) for 10 minutes at approximately 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and retain the cell pellets.
Resuspend the cell pellets in lysis buffer A using a pipette for HERC2ZZ and H31-6 linked and SUMO11-6 linked HERC2ZZ purification.
Resuspend the cell pellets in lysis buffer B for SUMO1 purification.
Lysate cells by sonication on ice for 10 minutes at 60% power with intervals of 5 seconds on and 10 seconds off.
Add lysozyme to the buffer if desired, to enhance lysis efficiency.
Add one tablet of EDTA-free protease inhibitor cocktail per liter of buffer.
Add DNAse I at a concentration of 10 μg/mL to inhibit protease activity and remove bound DNA.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 15,000 rpm (26,964 × g) for 30 minutes to remove debris and insoluble fractions.
Keep the cell lysate on ice during purification.
Incubate the supernatant with 3 mL Ni-NTA resin in a 50 mL Falcon tube for 1 hour rocking at 4°C.
Apply the suspension to an Econo-Pac® Chromatography Column to collect the protein-bound Ni-NTA resin.
Wash the resin with 20 mL of lysis buffer A.
Wash the resin with 40 mL of lysis buffer A containing 20 mM imidazole (pH 7.5).
Wash the resin again with 40 mL of lysis buffer A containing 30 mM imidazole (pH 7.5).
Take a 15 μL sample from each purification step.
Add 5 μL of 4X SDS loading buffer to each sample.
Heat samples to 90°C for 10 minutes to denature them.
Load the samples onto a 15-well 15% SDS PAGE gel (15% resolving, 5% stacking).
Prepare the gel and 4X SDS loading buffer according to standard Bio-Rad protocol.
Resuspend Ni-NTA resin in 10 mL lysis buffer A.
Add prepared Ulp1 enzyme (14 mg/mL, 30 μL) to the resuspended resin.
Incubate the mixture rocking on a Microplate Titer Plate Shaker at 4°C for 4–24 hours.
Analyze a 15 μL sample of the cleavage reaction by polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE).
Collect the cleavage supernatant once ∼60%–100% cleavage is achieved.
Concentrate the protein to 2 mL using a 3 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter at 3,000 × g.
Inject the concentrated protein onto a HiPrep™ 16/60 Sephacryl® S-100 HR column pre-equilibrated in gel-filtration buffer at 0.5 mL/min.
Pool fractions containing HERC2ZZ protein eluted around ∼85 mL on the column.
Concentrate pooled fractions to 5 mg/mL using a 3 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter at 3,000 × g.
Incubate the supernatant with 3 mL Glutathione Sepharose 4B beads for 3 hours rocking at 4°C.
Apply the bead-protein suspension to an Econo-Pac® Chromatography Column to collect the bound GST resin.
Wash the resin by passing through lysis buffer B (50 mL) through the column.
Resuspend the GST resin in 10 mL lysis buffer B.
Add prepared TEV enzyme (14 mg/mL, 30 μL) to the resuspended GST resin.
Incubate the reaction mixture gently rocking for 4–24 h at 4°C.
Analyze a 15 μL sample of cleavage supernatant as in step 14 to assess MW difference corresponding to protein cleavage.
Concentrate untagged SUMO1 to 2 mL using a 10 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter.
Inject the concentrated untagged SUMO1 onto an HiPrep™ 16/60 Sephacryl® S-100 HR column pre-equilibrated in gel-filtration buffer at 0.5 mL/min.
Prepare the protein samples for histone peptide pull-down.
Express HERC2ZZ following steps 1–4 in the section of HERC2ZZ and full-length SUMO1 expression and purification.
Resuspend the pellet from a 100 mL culture in 10 mL pre-chilled lysis buffer C.
Add 100 μL of 50 mg/mL lysozyme solution to the cells, keeping them on ice for 30 min with occasional inversion.
Sonicate the cells on ice using a Branson SFX250 sonicator at 18% power for 20 s with intervals of 1 s on and off; repeat twice.
Transfer the lysate into a 15 mL disposable tube and spin down at 12,000 rpm (13,000 × g) at 4°C for 15 min.
Transfer the supernatant (∼10 mL) of lysed bacteria to a new 15 mL tube.
Prepare glutathione beads.
For each 10 mL cell lysate, use 100 μL of glutathione agarose slurry for purification.
Mix the glutathione agarose slurry before use.
Add 10 mL of cold lysis buffer C.
Wash the beads at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 2,000 rpm (376 × g) at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the washing process with lysis buffer C two more times.
Bring the final volume of beads to 200 μL using lysis buffer C.
Add 200 μL of washed 50% slurry of glutathione beads into the cell lysates.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C with gentle rotation on a tube rotator (Lab Quake) at 20 rpm for 4 hours.
Centrifuge the tube at 2,000 rpm (376 × g) at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 10 mL of pre-chilled lysis buffer C.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C with rotation for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge to remove the supernatant.
Repeat this washing step twice more.
Add 10 mL of pre-chilled GST elution buffer (without glutathione) to the beads.
Centrifuge at 4,000 rpm (1,500 × g) for 1 minute to remove the supernatant.
Add 350 μL of GST elution buffer (with glutathione).
Incubate the mixture at 4°C with rotation for 4 hours.
Centrifuge at 4,000 rpm (1,500 × g) for 2 minutes.
Transfer 300 μL of supernatant into a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Determine the protein concentration by Bio-Rad Bradford assay.
Thaw GST-tagged proteins on ice.
Spin down thawed GST-tagged proteins at 13,000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Dilute GST-tagged proteins to a final volume of 300 μL per tube with binding buffer.
Prepare an additional tube of diluted GST-tagged protein as input control.
Add 1 μg of biotinylated histone peptides (1 mg/mL) into each tube containing diluted GST-tagged proteins.
Incubate the tubes at 4°C with rotation for 4 hours.
Wash Streptavidin Magnetic beads two times with binding buffer through agitation for 5 minutes on a tube rotator.
Resuspend washed magnetic beads in 10 μL of binding buffer.
Add 10 μL of resuspended magnetic beads into each tube and incubate at 4°C with rotation for 1 hour.
Wash the beads three times with 1 mL of binding buffer through rotation at 4°C for 5 minutes each.
Resuspend the washed beads in 60 μL of 2X SDS sample buffer.
Take 30 μL from the input tube and add 30 μL of 2X SDS sample buffer to it.
Heat the combined samples in boiling water.
Load 10 μL of each sample for Western blot analysis.
Ensure the quality and quantity of biotinylated histone peptides are equal by dot blot.
Validate the interaction between HERC2ZZ and its ligands by NMR spectroscopy.
Concentrate the 15N-labeled WT HERC2ZZ and mutant proteins to 0.1 mM in binding buffer.
Add 22 μL of deuterium oxide to 198 μL protein sample.
Transfer the sample to a Shigemi 5 mm symmetrical NMR microtube.
Record 1H,15N heteronuclear single quantum coherence (HSQC) spectra at 298K on a Varian INOVA 600 MHz NMR spectrometer.
Add increasing amounts of H31–12 or SUMO11–6 peptide to the NMR sample.
Record 1H,15N HSQC spectra after each addition until saturation is reached.
Process the spectra using NMRPipe software.
Overlay the spectra to reveal resonance perturbations induced by peptide binding.
Fill a quartz fluorometer cuvette with 400 μL of binding buffer A.
Record the spectrum of control in the fluorometer.
Excite the sample at 295 nm and record tryptophan emission spectra over wavelengths from 330 nm to 360 nm, using a step size of 0.5 nm and an integration time of 1 second, averaged over three scans.
Add HERC2ZZ protein into the binding buffer to achieve a final concentration of 5 μM.
Before adding the protein, remove an equal volume of buffer from the cuvette to maintain sample volume consistency.
Record spectra at 0 min, 5 min, and 10 min to ensure emission curves are stable before adding ligands.
Add increasing amounts of H31-12 or SUMO11-6 peptide to the protein sample.
Record spectra after each addition of the peptide.
Analyze the data using KaleidaGraph 4.5 software (or Prism 8, OriginPro).
Determine binding affinity through nonlinear least-squares analysis using the appropriate equation.
Culture HEK 293T cells in DMEM medium at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Perform plasmid transfection when HEK 293T cells reach 50%-60% confluence.
Transfect reactions in 500 μL Opti-MEM.
Use 2 μg of pcDNA-H3-3Flag, 4 μg of pcDNA-HERC (aa 2,702–2,755) and 18 μL X-tremeGENE™ HP DNA transfection reagent for experimental conditions.
Use 2 μg of pcDNA-flag vector, 4 μg of pcDNA-HERC (aa 2,702–2,755) plasmids and 18 μL X-tremeGENE™ HP DNA transfection reagent for control conditions.
Run an agarose gel before transfection to ensure plasmids are of high quality with a supercoil form.
Scrape cells 48 hours after transfection and resuspend in 1 mL cell lysis buffer.
Keep the cell lysate on ice for 30 minutes, flipping tubes gently.
Sonicate the cells on ice using a Branson SFX250 sonicator at 15% output with intervals of 1 second on and off for 30–40 seconds.
Spin the cells at 12,000 rpm (13,000 × g) for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant into a new 1.5 mL reaction tube.
Determine protein concentration in the lysate.
Save 50 μL of lysate as 5% input.
Use 30 μL of Flag M2 beads for each binding.
Wash flag beads three times with 10X volume of cell lysis buffer containing PMSF.
Rock the tubes on a tube rotator at 4°C for 5 minutes per wash and spin down the beads at 3,000 rpm (845 × g) for 2 minutes.
Resuspend the beads with same volume of cold cell lysis buffer after the last wash.
Add 30 μL of FLAG M2 beads into 950 μL of lysate using wide bore pipette tips.
Incubate the lysate with beads at 4°C with rotation for 4 hours, gently mixing until beads are fully resuspended (∼20 times).
Wash the beads four to five times with 1 mL cold cell lysis buffer.
Add 200 μL of 2X SDS sample buffer into the pellet after final wash.
For input, add 150 μL of 2X SDS sample buffer.
Heat all samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Load 10 μL sample for Western blot analysis.
Sonicate all samples at the same setting.
Close lids properly while mixing.
Remove wash supernatant with a pipette at an angle to avoid losing beads during wash steps.
Concentrate H31–6-HERC2ZZ and SUMO11–6-HERC2ZZ proteins to 3–5 mg/mL.
Spin down the concentrated proteins to remove precipitates.
Mix 1 μL of protein solution with 1 μL of reservoir solution for crystallization.
Place the mixture in a sitting drop vapor diffusion setup against 50 μL of reservoir solution at 25°C.
Grow H3-HERC2ZZ crystals in 0.1 M ammonium acetate, 0.1 M Bis-Tris, pH 5.5 and 17% PEG 10,000 condition.
Obtain SUMO1-HERC2ZZ crystals in 0.2 M ammonium chloride, 0.1 M Tris, pH 8.0 and 20% PEG 6,000 condition.
Wait for plate-shaped crystals to appear within 24 hours and grow them to full size within 2-3 days.
Transfer the crystals using appropriate loops under an optical microscope.
Cryoprotect the crystals with 25% glycerol before freezing in liquid nitrogen.
Collect crystallization data sets using a high-frequency microfocus X-ray generator.
Index, integrate, and scale crystallographic data using HKL2000 program.
Determine structures by molecular replacement using Molrep in CCP4.
Use P300ZZ (PDB code: 6DS6) as a search model for HERC2ZZ structures.
Perform model building with Coot.
Refine structures with Phenix Refine.
Validate the final model using Worldwide Protein Data Bank OneDep SYSTEM.
Deposit data in Worldwide Protein Data Bank OneDep SYSTEM.
